transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand there shaking like a leaf in a storm, but there is no wind here. The gold does not care about your trembling, and neither does the stone. Why have you come to disturb the quiet?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will give you ten years of my life if you open it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Time is a circle down here, little thing, not a line you can cut into pieces. Ten years of your life is a blink to the stone, and less than a breath to me. What would I do with your wrinkled skin and failing eyes?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then take my memory of the ocean. I won't remember the blue anymore, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I have tasted the salt of oceans that dried up before your great-grandfather was born. Your memory is small and cloudy, like water in a dirty cup. It is not a jewel that fits in this room.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take the sound of my mother's voice then. I’ll forget it right now.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You offer that so quickly, as if it burns your hands to hold it. A mother’s voice is usually the anchor that keeps your kind from drifting away, yet you would cut the rope. Is the voice so terrible, or are you just that foolish?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't need it. I just need to go inside.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need is a hunger, and hunger is boring because everyone has it. You are trying to buy a mountain with a handful of sand. You do not even know if you truly own the things you are trying to sell.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take my name. I won't be Salim, I'll be nobody.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A name is just a label on a jar, and if the jar is empty, the label is worth nothing. If you give me your name, I am talking to a ghost, and ghosts do not open heavy doors. You are offering me air.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I offer you my fear. Take all of it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fear is the common clay of this place, coating the walls and dripping into the river until everything smells of it. Why would I want your terror when I can breathe the panic of a thousand lost souls just by standing here? You offer me water while I am drowning in a flood.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take my eyes then. I don't need to see the way back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If I take your sight, you become nothing but a stumbling weight that I must guide through the tunnels. A blind servant is a burden, not a gift, and I do not carry burdens for anyone. You are trying to strip yourself to the bone, but your bones are soft.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't ever laugh again. You can have every laugh I have left.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The laughter of a terrified boy is a sharp, cracking sound that would only disturb the dust. I prefer the heavy silence of the stones to the noise of your forced joy. You offer me noise when I have no use for it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then take my breath. I’ll hold it until you let me through.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is a child’s tantrum, threatening to turn blue if the world does not bend to his wish. Do you think the gate cares if you suffocate on the doorstep? It has stood closed while entire kingdoms turned to sand above us.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I give you my future children. They won't exist, I promise.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You cannot give me what isn't real, handing me empty baskets and telling me they are full of harvest. You are trading in smoke and dreams because you have run out of things you can actually touch. It is a poor currency.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Take my shadow. Peel it off the floor and keep it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A shadow is just a hole in the light, and we have plenty of darkness down here without yours adding to it. You are emptying your pockets of lint and dust, hoping something shines. Stop throwing pieces of yourself at the wall.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have to give you something heavy enough to open it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You speak of heaviness, yet you are frantically throwing overboard everything that gives you weight. Tell me of this brother you followed; tell me the color of his eyes without trying to sell me the memory. Can you even do that?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I give you the color. I won't remember what he looks like if you just let me find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I asked for a simple truth, and you immediately wrapped it in a transaction and offered it like a rug merchant. You are so consumed by the deal that the boy himself has become nothing but currency to you. Do you even miss him, or do you just miss your own peace?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I miss him enough to give you everything! Take my peace, I don't want it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are not listening to me; you are only listening for the sound of the latch clicking open. If I asked you to tell me his favorite fear, you would only offer to take it onto yourself. You are hollowing yourself out until there is no Salim left to greet him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There doesn't need to be a Salim. There just needs to be an open door.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: But who walks through the door if you have traded away your legs, your eyes, and your name? A husk cannot lead another husk out of the dark, and I do not open my home to empty shells. You are dismantling the very vessel that is supposed to carry him home.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then take the rest of me! Take whatever parts are left.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are screaming at stone, thinking that volume will succeed where value failed. Let us try one last time to find something solid in this mist. What is the last thing you said to him before the hand took him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him. Take the dare, take the words back, make it so I never said them.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You still cannot just answer; you must try to undo the past as if it were a knot in a rope. The past is the stone we stand on, and you cannot sell the floor from under your own feet. You are bankrupt, little one.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not bankrupt. I still have my life to give.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A life given is just a corpse on my doorstep, and I have no shortage of those. You offer your death as a solution, but a dead brother is of no use to the one waiting in the dark. You are trying to pay a debt with counterfeit coin, and the vault knows the difference.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then take the years off the end. Make me old right now.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You negotiate with time as if you held the hourglass in your own trembling hands. I wanted to see the courage that brought you down here, but you have buried it under a mountain of frantic bids. You are not a warrior anymore; you are just a desperate merchant selling things he does not own.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not a merchant. I'm just trying to pay the price.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: But you do not know the price, so you offer the moon and the stars and hope one of them satisfies me. You are so busy selling yourself that you have forgotten to actually be here. There is no one left inside your skin to greet him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There is. I'm still inside.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Are you? If I asked you his name now, you would probably offer to sell me the letters just to see the hinges move. You have hollowed yourself out, little one, and the gate does not open for empty vessels.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: His name is Omar. I didn't sell it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You said it, but you did not feel it; it was just another stone thrown at the wall to see if it would break. You have stripped away everything that made you Salim, and I cannot grant passage to a ghost. You have faded away while we were talking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am not a ghost. Open it, please.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The door is heavy, and it requires a whole person to move it, not a scattering of panic and bargaining chips. You are not solid enough to cross this threshold today. Come back when you are real again.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm solid enough. Just turn the lock.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The lock does not respond to fingers that are shaking this violently. You are vibrating with so much fear that you have blurred the edges of who you are. You are a smudge in the air, not a man.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can stop shaking. Just give me a second to stand still.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It is not your hands that tremble, but your intent; you are throwing words at me blindly to see which ones stick. You are not a brother right now. You are a marketplace of panic trying to sell its own walls.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not a marketplace. I'm just someone who needs to get through.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: But you are not someone; you are a collection of desperate offers held together by skin. If I opened the gate, the wind from the abyss would blow you apart like dried leaves. There is no weight left in you to hold the ground.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let it blow me apart then. I don't care what happens to me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: And that is precisely why the door stays shut; you value the passage so much you have forgotten to value the traveler. A nothing cannot save a something. I do not let the wind in to chase the darkness.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not nothing. I am Salim.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say the name, but it sounds like a question you are asking me to answer. You have bartered away your certainty until you are just a shape in the dark waiting to be told it exists. You have faded.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know who I am. I am the one who is going to save Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are the one who is leaving, because there is not enough of you here to stay. The stone is sealing itself, little ghost; come back when you have a face I can recognize. The hall is closed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No, don't close it! I'm real, I promise I'm real!
